{{No footnotes|date=August 2025}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''transverse knot''' is a smooth [[embedding]] of a [[circle (topology)|circle]] into a three-dimensional [[contact manifold]] such that the [[tangent vector]] at every point of the knot is [[transversality theorem|transverse]] to the contact plane at that point.

Any [[Legendrian knot]] can be ''C''<sup>0</sup>-perturbed in a direction transverse to the contact planes to obtain a transverse knot.  This yields a [[bijection]] between the set of [[isomorphism]] classes of transverse knots and the set of isomorphism classes of Legendrian knots [[Equivalence relation|modulo]] negative Legendrian stabilization.
